content.statement: After Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, Articles 14, 19 and 21 are read together so that a procedure depriving life or personal liberty must be fair, just and reasonable, and restrictions engaging those articles are not analysed in isolated silos.
elements: Article 21 procedure must be fair, just and reasonable
Article 19 freedoms are considered where a citizen’s freedoms are also engaged
content.development: Maneka Gandhi (1978) 1 SCC 248 rejected the rigid compartmentalisation associated with A.K. Gopalan.
content.application: When liberty or a citizen freedom is curtailed, analyse 14–19–21 together rather than Article 21 alone.
